title: PowerPoint for Mac: start a Copilot presentation from PowerPoint Home
summary: Hold: the Mac device-preference row reports no admin interface even though Microsoft documents deployment through Intune. Its automation text names a preference and value, not a callable operation. The rollout, default state and cautiously qualified licensing discussion are supported.

claims.quote: You can now create a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint straight from the PowerPoint Home in file menu.

claims.claim: The new entry point avoids having to open a blank or existing file first.
claims.quote: This update reduces friction at the start of the workflow, helping users move from idea to first draft faster without needing to open a new file.

claims.claim: The experience is available immediately when PowerPoint is opened.

claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Mac PowerPoint Home Copilot 560536 Basic license; PowerPoint Mac Home Basic Copilot. Read overview and release notes, including Home references; explicit Basic/Premium entry is Web. MC1311973 names licensed Mac users.

claims.claim: No meter or credit charge specific to this entry point is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home Copilot create presentation credit charge pricing meter Mac; PowerPoint Copilot Home price. Read overview, release notes and returned excerpts; none names a Home-entry-point meter or credit charge.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no price specific to this entry point.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Home Copilot create presentation credit charge pricing meter Mac; PowerPoint Copilot Home price. Read overview, release notes and returned excerpts; no entry-point-specific price.

claims.claim: No new licence specific to this entry point is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Mac PowerPoint Home Copilot 560536 Basic license; PowerPoint Mac Home Basic Copilot. Read overview, release notes and MC1311973; the notice names an existing Microsoft Copilot license, not a new entry-point licence.

claims.claim: No tenant UI or API specifically hides the PowerPoint Home Copilot entry point on its own.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Mac PowerPoint Home Copilot 560536 hide disable entry point policy; PowerPoint Home Copilot hide. Read Copilot settings, Mac privacy preferences, suite-wide Mac preferences, Cloud Policy overview; no entry-point-only switch.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy reaches the named content-analysis setting through Customization, Policy Management, Create, Choose the scope and Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Start with the basics page, enter a name (required) and a description (optional), then select Next.
claims.fix: Use 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content'. Both cited pages were read: the Cloud Policy overview supplies the route; mac-privacy-preferences supplies the setting and links to that route. The omitted page headings and basic fields are not blocking choices.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for configuring this setting through Cloud Policy itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service API Microsoft Graph configure OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference; Cloud Policy API configuration; Cloud Policy Graph create Microsoft 365 Apps. Read Cloud Policy overview and returned excerpts; found no Cloud Policy write API.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin UI for deploying the Mac content-analysis preference.
claims.quote: Select Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy. Platform: Select macOS. Profile type: Select Templates > Preference file. In Configuration settings, configure your settings: Preference domain name; Property list file.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].ui null with surface 'Microsoft Intune admin center', path 'Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > macOS > Templates > Preference file > Create > Basics > Configuration settings > Property list file', and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-configuration/templates/configure-preference-file-macos. In the note state: 'For Intune-enrolled, MDM-managed Macs; Policy and Profile Manager role. Set Preference domain name to com.microsoft.office and upload preference XML setting OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference to Boolean FALSE.' Cite that page and the existing Mac privacy-preferences reference.

claims.claim: com.microsoft.office OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference FALSE (Configuration Profile or MDM) is an automation call that sets this control.
claims.quote: Searched: OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference defaults; OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference Intune. Read Mac privacy preferences, Intune preference-file guidance and Graph macOSCustomAppConfiguration update. The printed tuple is not an operation.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api with kind 'graph', call 'PATCH /beta/deviceManagement/deviceConfigurations/{deviceConfigurationId}', and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/intune-deviceconfig-macoscustomappconfiguration-update?view=graph-rest-beta. Add to its note: 'For an existing assigned Intune macOSCustomAppConfiguration, the request body sets bundleId to com.microsoft.office and configurationXml to the UTF-8 preference XML containing OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference with Boolean FALSE. This is an Intune beta API and requires an active Intune licence.' Retain the verified enforcement explanation; remove the domain/key/value tuple from the call.

claims.quote: Preference setting for connected experiences that analyze your content; Preference Domain: com.microsoft.office

claims.quote: Key: OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference

claims.where: controls[2].api; controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Boolean FALSE disables the Mac content-analysis preference and makes Copilot features unavailable in certain apps.
claims.quote: Data Type: Boolean; Possible values: TRUE (enabled) FALSE (disabled). If you set this preference to FALSE, Microsoft Copilot features won’t be available to your users in certain apps.

claims.claim: Configuration Profile or MDM enforcement prevents users changing the preference.
claims.quote: These new preference settings are CFPreferences API compatible and can be set using the defaults command in Terminal, or enforced through a Configuration Profile or Mobile Device Management (MDM) server. When the preferences are enforced, the user can't change the values

claims.claim: The content-analysis control also covers experiences such as PowerPoint Designer.
claims.quote: Connected experiences that analyze your content are experiences that use your Office content to provide you with design recommendations, editing suggestions, data insights, and similar features. For example, PowerPoint Designer or Researcher in Word.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off content-analysis connected experiences makes Copilot unavailable in Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word on Mac, rather than only at this entry point.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: Excel; OneNote; Outlook; PowerPoint; Word. This applies to ... Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: Creating Cloud Policy settings requires the Office Apps admin role.
claims.quote: For example, creating Cloud Policy settings for Microsoft 365 apps requires the Office Apps admin role.
claims.fix: Replace the exclusive role requirement with 'Office Apps Administrator is the recommended role for Cloud Policy; the Cloud Policy overview also lists Security Administrator and Global Administrator as supported roles.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy, whose Supported built-in admin roles table lists all three; retain the Copilot settings page as the source of the differing wording.

claims.claim: An appropriate role such as AI Administrator can manage Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center, use an appropriate admin role, such as AI Administrator.

claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section
